text:
Aya (Support): heads up — AcmePay just escalated: per-model throughput panels in Console are showing flatlines (QPS = 0) for ~40 models since the metric push last night. Their app is still serving traffic (customer logs + request traces show normal qps). Screenshot attached in ticket #12345. Can someone triage? :grimacing:
grafana-bot: ALERT: 'per-model-throughput' panels have zero series for label 'model' since 2024-11-02T22:10Z.
Marisol (CS): Customer is on Dedicated prod in us-west-2, flagged P1. They need a quick workaround while you triage.
Jun (Eng SRE): thx — can you paste the Promql panels or the raw query the dashboard uses and an example model name that’s flatlined?
Aya (Support): panel query from Console: `sum(rate(redwood_serving_requests_total{job="redwood_exporter"}[5m])) by (model)`
Example model: `gpt-infer-32k-v2` — customer traces show ~120 qps but panel shows 0.
Liam (Metrics): we rolled out an exporter relabeling last night to standardize keys: old label `model` -> new label `model_name`. The exporter now emits `model_name` only. Looks like dashboards still use `model`. Essentially the metric exists but with a different label key, so `by(model)` returns no series.
Jun (Eng SRE): ok that explains symptoms. Two mitigation approaches: 1) quickly modify dashboards to reference `model_name` OR 2) add a compatibility relabeling/recording rule to restore `model`. Which is less risky for Dedicated customers?
Marisol (CS): Customer prefers we restore the old key so dashboard and alerts keep working. They don’t want dashboard edits on their side.
ops-oncall: agree — short lived compatibility layer is best. Liam, can you add a recording rule or a prometheus relabel to copy `model_name` -> `model`? ETA?
Liam (Metrics): I can push a recording rule to the central Prometheus for Dedicated regions. Quick rule: `- record: redwood_serving_requests_total_compat\n  expr: sum by (instance, job, model_name)(rate(redwood_serving_requests_total{job="redwood_exporter"}[5m]))\n` then expose a metric with label `model` via relabeling. But easier: add a metric_relabel_config on the exporter scrape that sets `model` from `model_name`. Example (prometheus scrape config snippet):
```
- job_name: redwood_exporter
  static_configs:
  - targets: ['exporter-0.redwood.svc:9100']
  metric_relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [model_name]
    target_label: model
    action: replace
```
This will make `model` present again for existing panels.
Jun (Eng SRE): note — if we do scrape-level relabeling we won't duplicate time series, but if both `model` and `model_name` exist we risk duplication. Use action: replace so it only sets model when missing.
Liam (Metrics): good point. I'll craft a patch for the prometheus-operator configmap with `metric_relabel_configs` targeted at the dedicated exporters in us-west-2 first. ETA 12-15m to apply and roll.
Aya (Support): relayed to customer: we have a short mitigation plan, ETA ~20m to restore dashboard visibility. Customer ok with that.
ops-oncall: make sure to check for recording rules that power billing / long-term aggregation — we should not break downstream consumers.
Liam (Metrics): will verify. Also will update Console dashboards to query `coalesce(label_replace(redwood_serving_requests_total, "model", "$1", "model_name", "(.+)") , model)` as a follow-up so dashboards are tolerant of either label.
Jun (Eng SRE): if you can include the exact kubectl apply patch you used (or PR link) we can track and revert cleanly after compatibility window.
Liam (Metrics): pasted the patch I applied to prometheus configmap in staging and then prod (us-west-2):
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  prometheus.yml: |-
    scrape_configs:
    - job_name: redwood_exporter
      kubernetes_sd_configs: ...
      metric_relabel_configs:
      - source_labels: [model_name]
        target_label: model
        action: replace
```
Applied via `kubectl apply -f prometheus-configmap-usw2.yml` then reloaded Prometheus.
Jun (Eng SRE): nice — any rollout blips?
Liam (Metrics): none observed, Prometheus reload picked up new config. I can see series reappearing in Prometheus: `sum by (model)(rate(redwood_serving_requests_total[5m]))` returning non-zero now.
Marisol (CS): customer confirmed panels now have lines back and throughput numbers look sane. They appreciate the quick fix.
ops-oncall: please add a short postmortem note in #incidents and include timeline + plan to update dashboards to use both keys or migrate fully. Also schedule deprecation announcement for `model` -> `model_name` with at least 2 weeks notice.
Liam (Metrics): will open PR with dashboard tolerant query changes and a deprecation communication.
Aya (Support): marking ticket #12345 as pending verification, will close after customer confirms a few hours of stable graphs. Thanks all. :tada:
